raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Opts `NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` into vLLM's existing `mm_device_do_normalize` path, so the fixed 2048x1664 canvas travels to the device as `uint8` and the rescale/normalize happens in `FusedMMInputNorm` instead of as single-threaded CPU work inside the engine process.

Please do aware this change depends on pending tied embedding fix for nemoparse2.0 embedding.

The checkpoint ships its image processor as remote code, and its `preprocess(self, images, return_tensors=None, **kwargs)` **ignores** the `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs that `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` injects when the feature is on: it always runs `ToTensor` and normalizes from `self.do_normalize`. Setting the model flag alone would therefore normalize twice. The `_call_hf_processor` override replays the processor's own pipeline up to (but not including) `ToTensor` to produce the raw canvas, and raises -- pointing at `--no-mm-device-do-normalize` -- if a checkpoint does not expose that pipeline, so "feature on => `uint8`" holds by construction.

## Claims

- `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True`; `build_mm_input_norm()` builds the norm and `_process_image_input` applies it unconditionally, as in the other models that opt in. With the feature off that is `IdentityInputNorm`, i.e. a plain cast.
- With the feature off, behaviour is identical to today.
- Both published checkpoints are handled: v1.2 (albumentations `transform` branch) and 2.0 (`_pad_to_size` branch).
- Payload per request drops 40.89 MB fp32 -> 10.22 MB uint8.

## Validation

Run on the latest `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` = `0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`, whose `nemotron_parse.py` is byte-identical to this patch's parent and whose `layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py` is byte-identical to this branch -- so the Triton `forward_cuda`, `IdentityInputNorm` and `_load_norm_params` exercised here are the ones this change targets. One H100, `--dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 --max-num-seqs 16`.

Greedy request on a sample document page (`max_tokens 512, temperature 0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, skip_special_tokens false`):

| engine | flag | dtype at model | `input_norm` | output sha256[:16] | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| patched | on | `uint8` | `FusedMMInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| patched | off | `bfloat16` | `IdentityInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | off | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | on | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |

Unpatched + on logs `Model does not support mm_device_do_normalize, forcing ... False`, confirming the flag is the only opt-in.

**Numerics** -- device path vs the host path it replaces:

| case | bf16 | fp16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| real page, 10,223,616 elements | **equal, 0 mismatched** | equal, 0 | max abs 2.4e-07 |
| all 3x256 possible byte values | **equal, 0 mismatched** | 3 at 1 ULP | max abs 4.8e-07 |
| `forward_cuda` vs `forward_native` | equal, 0 | equal, 0 | max abs 1.2e-07 |



**Latency**, 3 interleaved reps per arm, fresh server each, identical flags:

| | encoder-only p50 (`max_tokens=1`) | c=1 p50 | c=8 aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | **132.5 ms** | **131.8 ms** | 937.9 tok/s |
| off | 263.1 ms | 261.5 ms | 772.7 tok/s |

**1.99x**, with the per-rep ranges non-overlapping across all six reps, and +21% aggregate throughput at c=8. 

The win is, An isolated single-threaded CPU microbenchmark attributes the win: the processor's float work goes 160.3 ms -> 5.9 ms.

The added `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_parse.py` passes (2 passed).

Re-verified after making `input_norm` unconditional, same nightly, one H100: both flag arms produce identical output (`b37da04a78014080`, 5 greedy reps each), TTFT p50 226.8 -> 118.6 ms. With the feature off the unconditional call is bit-identical to the `pixel_values.to(dtype)` it replaces -- 0 differing elements of 10,223,616, in bf16, fp16 and fp32 -- so the default path is unchanged. Deleting `_resize_with_aspect_ratio` or `_pad_to_size` from the processor raises a `RuntimeError` naming `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Details

`_build_uint8_canvas` depends on three attributes of the checkpoint's remote-code image processor: `_resize_with_aspect_ratio`, `_pad_to_size` and `transform`. Two are private by convention and none is a stable API. If they change, the lookup raises and the error names `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`, so the failure is loud instead of a silent loss of the speedup. The cleaner fix lives in the checkpoint: `preprocess` should honour its own `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs, after which this override can be deleted entirely. I am happy to drop the override and gate the feature on that instead if reviewers prefer.

Reproducing the `b37da04a78014080` output on `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` additionally requires the tied-`lm_head` fix (#60272, a re-land of #53020); without it that checkpoint's output head is randomly initialized and the server emits garbage while reporting healthy. That fix is independent of this change and was applied only for the validation runs above.

Not covered: CUDA only (`forward_xpu` / `forward_oot` are untouched and untested); one image per request, which is this model's `get_supported_mm_limits`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Using dtype to distinguish between the cases seems hacky, why can't we just call input_norm unconditionally like in the other models?
It's fine to just import this directly

Beyond the two inline findings, I also looked at the ">210 concurrent images crashes the engine" concern raised earlier on `_process_image_input`'s Triton norm call: that limit lives in the shared `mm_input_norm.py` kernel (unmodified by this PR, already exercised by qwen2_vl/glm4_1v/qwen2_5_vl/kimi_k25 which also set `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True`), so it's pre-existing shared-infra behavior rather than a new risk introduced by this change.


<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

Checked whether the large-batch Triton-kernel crash concern (previously raised inline and now resolved) is specific to this diff; `mm_input_norm.py` is untouched here and the same kernel already backs several other merged models with the same opt-in flag, so the exposure is not new. That leaves the two confirmed correctness findings (PIL-only assumption in `_build_uint8_canvas` breaking numpy/tensor image inputs, and the uint8-canvas branch triggering on explicit per-request do_rescale/do_normalize kwargs regardless of whether mm_device_do_normalize is actually enabled) as the open items for this PR.

</details>

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.

<!-- bhrv:cebd91703170a96b -->

🔴 Nemotron-Parse now crashes on valid image inputs that are numpy arrays or torch tensors instead of parsing them, because mm_device_do_normalize defaults to True and this model now opts in. _build_uint8_canvas (nemotron_parse.py:426) calls image.convert('RGB'), a PIL-only method; the resulting AttributeError is caught by _call_hf_processor (nemotron_parse.py:471-477) and re-raised as a RuntimeError blaming the checkpoint's remote code and suggesting --no-mm-device-do-normalize, hiding the real cause. Fix: convert any non-PIL array/tensor image item to a PIL image before calling .convert(), so this previously-working input type keeps working with the feature on by default.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A caller passes multi_modal_data={'image': <np.ndarray>} or a non-embedding 3-D torch.Tensor image, a shape vllm/multimodal/parse.py's _parse_image_data (around line 753) and HfImageItem (vllm/multimodal/inputs.py:38) explicitly support. mm_device_do_normalize defaults True (vllm/config/multimodal.py:352) and NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration now sets supports_mm_device_do_normalize=True (nemotron_parse.py:613), so by default _call_hf_processor takes the uint8-canvas branch (nemotron_parse.py:456-480). _build_uint8_canvas's image.convert('RGB') (line 426) raises AttributeError for ndarray/Tensor, caught and turned into a RuntimeError pointing at --no-mm-device-do-normalize, instead of succeeding as it did pre-change when the real remote preprocess (a generic HF-style processor tolerating PIL/array/tensor) ran.

**Verification:** By default this model now takes the uint8-canvas branch, which crashes on numpy/torch image inputs that the base branch handled. _build_uint8_canvas at nemotron_parse.py:426 does np.asarray(image.convert("RGB")); .convert is PIL-only, so it raises AttributeError, caught at nemotron_parse.py:471-477 and re-raised as a RuntimeError blaming the checkpoint's remote code.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) NemotronParseMultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor decides to build the raw uint8 canvas purely from the merged do_rescale/do_normalize kwargs, never checking whether mm_device_do_normalize is actually enabled. If a caller sets mm_processor_kwargs do_rescale=False/do_normalize=False while mm_device_do_normalize is off (e.g. --no-mm-device-do-normalize), the override still returns a raw uint8 canvas, but self.input_norm is IdentityInputNorm (just a dtype cast), so the encoder gets unnormalized pixel data with no error. Fix: gate the canvas shortcut on the model's multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize flag itself, not only on the resulting do_rescale/do_normalize values, so it only fires when the device-norm feature is truly active.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request or server config sets mm_processor_kwargs={'do_rescale': False, 'do_normalize': False} while --no-mm-device-do-normalize is in effect (or the checkpoint's supports_mm_device_do_normalize path is otherwise disabled). _call_hf_processor (nemotron_parse.py:454-465) only inspects merged_kwargs['do_rescale']/['do_normalize'] via get_merged_mm_kwargs, not multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize. It then builds a uint8 HWC canvas and skips the real preprocess. build_mm_input_norm (mm_input_norm.py:349) returns IdentityInputNorm when mm_device_do_normalize is False, so _process_image_input (nemotron_parse.py:686) only casts dtype, no rescale/normalize. The encoder silently receives raw 0-255 pixel values instead of normalized floats, producing incorrect/garbage output with no exception, whereas on base branch do_rescale/do_normalize had no effect at all since the remote processor ignores them and always normalized correctly.

**Verification:** nit. The code path is real and demonstrable. `_call_hf_processor` (nemotron_parse.py:454-465) decides to build the uint8 canvas purely from `not merged_kwargs.get("do_rescale", True)` and `not merged_kwargs.get("do_normalize", True)`, never checking `mm_device_do_normalize`. `merge_mm_processor_kwargs` (config/multimodal.py:724-734) forces those two flags to False only when `self.mm_device_do_normalize` is truthy; when device-norm is off a user's explicit `mm_processor_kwargs={'do_rescale': False, 'do_normalize': False}` passes through unchanged.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for Nemotron-Parse's device-side normalisation path."""
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+from PIL import Image
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.mm_input_norm import build_mm_input_norm
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+from ...utils import build_model_context
+
+_MODEL_ID = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0"
+
+
+def _noise_image(width: int, height: int) -> Image.Image:
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
+    return Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 256, (height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("default_vllm_config")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("width", "height"), [(1240, 1754), (310, 470)])
+def test_mm_device_do_normalize(width: int, height: int):
+    device = current_platform.device_type
+    ctx = build_model_context(_MODEL_ID, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1})
+    assert ctx.model_config.multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize
+
+    images = [_noise_image(width, height)]
+    prompt = [0]
+
+    ctx.model_config.multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize = False
+    processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(ctx.model_config)
+    mm_items = processor.info.parse_mm_data({"image": images})
+    normalized_values = processor(prompt, mm_items=mm_items)["mm_kwargs"].get_data()[
+        "pixel_values"
+    ]
+
+    ctx.model_config.multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize = True
+    processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(ctx.model_config)
+    raw_values = processor(prompt, mm_items=mm_items)["mm_kwargs"].get_data()[
+        "pixel_values"
+    ]
+    assert raw_values.dtype == torch.uint8
+    assert raw_values.shape == normalized_values.shape
+
+    input_norm = build_mm_input_norm(ctx.model_config).to(device)
+    output = input_norm(raw_values.flatten(1).to(device), normalized_values.dtype)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        output, normalized_values.flatten(1).to(device), rtol=1.6e-2, atol=1e-5
+    )

+def _build_uint8_canvas(
+    image_processor: Any, images: Sequence["Image.Image"]
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reproduce the image processor's pipeline up to, but excluding, its
+    `ToTensor` rescale, yielding the padded `uint8` canvas as `(N, 3, H, W)`.
+
+    Raises `AttributeError`/`TypeError` if the checkpoint's remote code does
+    not expose that pipeline.
+    """
+    resize = image_processor._resize_with_aspect_ratio
+    pad = image_processor._pad_to_size
+    # v1.x pads with albumentations, 2.0 sets `transform` to None and pads
+    # with `_pad_to_size`; mirror `preprocess` and pick the same branch.
+    transform = image_processor.transform
+
+    canvases = []
+    for image in images:
+        array = np.asarray(image.convert("RGB"))
+        array = resize(array)
+        array = transform(image=array)["image"] if transform is not None else pad(array)
+        if array.dtype != np.uint8 or array.ndim != 3 or array.shape[2] != 3:
+            raise TypeError(
+                f"expected a uint8 HWC canvas, got {array.dtype} {array.shape}"
+            )
+        canvases.append(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(array)).permute(2, 0, 1))
+
+    return torch.stack(canvases)
+

inline_comments.body: Using dtype to distinguish between the cases seems hacky, why can't we just call input_norm unconditionally like in the other models?
It's fine to just import this directly

🔴 Nemotron-Parse now crashes on valid image inputs that are numpy arrays or torch tensors instead of parsing them, because mm_device_do_normalize defaults to True and this model now opts in. _build_uint8_canvas (nemotron_parse.py:426) calls image.convert('RGB'), a PIL-only method; the resulting AttributeError is caught by _call_hf_processor (nemotron_parse.py:471-477) and re-raised as a RuntimeError blaming the checkpoint's remote code and suggesting --no-mm-device-do-normalize, hiding the real cause. Fix: convert any non-PIL array/tensor image item to a PIL image before calling .convert(), so this previously-working input type keeps working with the feature on by default.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A caller passes multi_modal_data={'image': <np.ndarray>} or a non-embedding 3-D torch.Tensor image, a shape vllm/multimodal/parse.py's _parse_image_data (around line 753) and HfImageItem (vllm/multimodal/inputs.py:38) explicitly support. mm_device_do_normalize defaults True (vllm/config/multimodal.py:352) and NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration now sets supports_mm_device_do_normalize=True (nemotron_parse.py:613), so by default _call_hf_processor takes the uint8-canvas branch (nemotron_parse.py:456-480). _build_uint8_canvas's image.convert('RGB') (line 426) raises AttributeError for ndarray/Tensor, caught and turned into a RuntimeError pointing at --no-mm-device-do-normalize, instead of succeeding as it did pre-change when the real remote preprocess (a generic HF-style processor tolerating PIL/array/tensor) ran.

**Verification:** By default this model now takes the uint8-canvas branch, which crashes on numpy/torch image inputs that the base branch handled. _build_uint8_canvas at nemotron_parse.py:426 does np.asarray(image.convert("RGB")); .convert is PIL-only, so it raises AttributeError, caught at nemotron_parse.py:471-477 and re-raised as a RuntimeError blaming the checkpoint's remote code.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) NemotronParseMultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor decides to build the raw uint8 canvas purely from the merged do_rescale/do_normalize kwargs, never checking whether mm_device_do_normalize is actually enabled. If a caller sets mm_processor_kwargs do_rescale=False/do_normalize=False while mm_device_do_normalize is off (e.g. --no-mm-device-do-normalize), the override still returns a raw uint8 canvas, but self.input_norm is IdentityInputNorm (just a dtype cast), so the encoder gets unnormalized pixel data with no error. Fix: gate the canvas shortcut on the model's multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize flag itself, not only on the resulting do_rescale/do_normalize values, so it only fires when the device-norm feature is truly active.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: a request or server config sets mm_processor_kwargs={'do_rescale': False, 'do_normalize': False} while --no-mm-device-do-normalize is in effect (or the checkpoint's supports_mm_device_do_normalize path is otherwise disabled). _call_hf_processor (nemotron_parse.py:454-465) only inspects merged_kwargs['do_rescale']/['do_normalize'] via get_merged_mm_kwargs, not multimodal_config.mm_device_do_normalize. It then builds a uint8 HWC canvas and skips the real preprocess. build_mm_input_norm (mm_input_norm.py:349) returns IdentityInputNorm when mm_device_do_normalize is False, so _process_image_input (nemotron_parse.py:686) only casts dtype, no rescale/normalize. The encoder silently receives raw 0-255 pixel values instead of normalized floats, producing incorrect/garbage output with no exception, whereas on base branch do_rescale/do_normalize had no effect at all since the remote processor ignores them and always normalized correctly.

**Verification:** nit. The code path is real and demonstrable. `_call_hf_processor` (nemotron_parse.py:454-465) decides to build the uint8 canvas purely from `not merged_kwargs.get("do_rescale", True)` and `not merged_kwargs.get("do_normalize", True)`, never checking `mm_device_do_normalize`. `merge_mm_processor_kwargs` (config/multimodal.py:724-734) forces those two flags to False only when `self.mm_device_do_normalize` is truthy; when device-norm is off a user's explicit `mm_processor_kwargs={'do_rescale': False, 'do_normalize': False}` passes through unchanged.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

That leaves the two confirmed correctness findings (PIL-only assumption in `_build_uint8_canvas` breaking numpy/tensor image inputs, and the uint8-canvas branch triggering on explicit per-request do_rescale/do_normalize kwargs regardless of whether mm_device_do_normalize is actually enabled) as the open items for this PR.
